sentences.text: This dinosaur was a relatively large member of the oviraptorid family, reaching a body length of more than 2 meters.
A unique anatomical feature involves the lower condyles of the quadrate bone being positioned below its upper head.
The first finger bone is notably long and slender, with a width across the palm equal to one-fifth of its total length.
Claws on the hand possess prominent lips located on the upper rear section of their tips.
The opening on the top of the skull roof is circular and significantly smaller than the opening found on the side of the cranium.
This species was one of eighteen dinosaur taxa described in 2015 within open access or free-to-read journals.
The genus was named and described in 2015 by a research team led by Lü Junchang and Pu Hanyong.
The name Huanansaurus comes from Huanan, the historical designation for Southern China.
The specific name ganzhouensis indicates the fossil's origin in the city of Ganzhou.
The primary specimen, cataloged as HGM41HIII-0443, originates from the Campanian-Maastrichtian layers of the Nanxiong Formation.
This holotype includes a partially articulated skeleton featuring a nearly complete skull, lower jaws, neck vertebrae, forelimb bones, and parts of the hindlimb.
The main specimen is currently kept at the Henan Geological Museum in Zhengzhou.
Another specimen, preserved resting on top of a nest, is held at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.
Taxonomically, this animal belongs to the family Oviraptoridae.
It is placed within the subfamily Oviraptorinae.
Research suggests it is a sister genus to Citipati inside the subfamily Oviraptorinae.
However, the Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of this species as Citipatinae.
Huanansaurus lived approximately 72 million years ago during the late Cretaceous period in what is now China.
It is debated whether Corythoraptor jacobsi is a synonym of Huanansaurus, as noted in 2017.
